back: Measuring the amplitude of a sound wave at regular time intervals and storing each value in binary.
Number of samples per second (Hz). Higher → more accurate sound, larger file.
Bits per sample. Higher → more amplitude levels ($2^n$), more accurate, larger file.
The smallest single-coloured element of a bitmap image.
Number of pixels (width × height). Higher → more detail, larger file.
Bits per pixel. $n$ bits → $2^n$ colours; higher → more realistic, larger file.
Data about the image, such as width, height and colour depth, stored so it can be rebuilt.
Visible blocks when a low-resolution image is enlarged: too few pixels for the size.
